exposure: Combination of intracervical Foley catheter and intracervical Dinoprostone gel
outcome: Duration of the latent phase of labour
Proportion of patients delivering within 12 hours
cohort: The study included 150 pregnant mothers, divided into two groups of 75 each, who required induction of labour at a tertiary care institution.
finding: The combination of Foley catheter with intracervical Dinoprostone gel did not prove to be more efficient than intracervical Dinoprostone alone for labour induction, with no significant differences in induction to delivery time, CS rates, neonatal outcomes, or labour complications.
mod_finding: The rates of Caesarean Sections (CS) were unaffected by the mode of induction, indicating no difference in the primary outcome of delivery method between the two intervention groups.
